goal: Show-me: the hook and the compelling question, the six-step cycle card, then the teacher thinks aloud from a broad topic and a short overview to an interesting part of it, two or three questions with a predicted answer, and a research plan: what I already know, what I still need, which sources I will try and in what order
note: Skill card "big topic, my part, questions, guess, plan; same words, three kinds, what each gave", held by the teacher. Hook: a photo of an Arctic fox in snow with "Where does it go in winter?" under it. No readiness check: every row the unit assumes was used in library grade 3, so it opens as retrieval on days 2 and 3. Candidates kept: the plan sheet's first lines "what the overview told me" and "what I still do not know" (the gaps cell, about 2 minutes), and a "when" box beside each plan step (the template and timeline cell, about 1 minute). Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): narrow one new broad topic to a part and write one question with a guess. Leans on the continuum's 3 to 5 band file, on disk, read by the frame and checked by the expert 2026-11-26 (its store entry waits on later.csv L149).

goal: Show-me: one narrowed question searched three ways with the same key words (the printed catalog page, an invented children's encyclopedia entry, an invented results page), what each kind gave written on the search plan, and inside a found book the contents, index and glossary used to reach the part that answers
note: Opens with the five-minute retrieval task: key words and a synonym for one question, and one scenario card, what to do and why (g3-key-words, g3-safe-searching, library grade 3), before the three-way search that uses them; where many miss it, the ten-minute reteach is grade 3's show-me case. The search plan gains one line today: "which kind, and what it gave". Stop rule on any search (close, tell, no blame); printed kinds or a teacher-checked page only (APPROACH Sensitive ground items 2 and 3). Paper path: all three kinds printed; a school with one projector may show a teacher-checked results page instead: the teacher checks the page the same day, and the printed results page is the swap. Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): say which of three kinds suits a new question and why.

goal: Practice: pairs with the card narrow two new broad topics to a part with questions and a guess, then search one question three ways in the printed kinds and record what each gave, with feedback after each round
note: Opens with the five-minute retrieval task: three research questions on a picture, one marked thick (g3-research-questions, library grade 3), before the narrowing practice. Pairs hold the card; every move was shown on days 1 and 2. Stop rule on any search (close, tell, no blame); printed kinds or a teacher-checked page only (APPROACH Sensitive ground items 2 and 3). Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): fix a plan whose sources do not fit its questions.

goal: Inquiry: for the host question, a narrowed part, questions with a guess and a plan, a search in two printed kinds with what each found recorded, the answering part read, who made it and why named, a one-line answer with its source line, a partner reads the plan and hears the answer, then the self-check
note: Card withdrawn today. Minutes: plan about 6, search two kinds about 10, judge and answer about 5, partner about 3, self-check about 4. Day 4 most often runs on the stand-alone Arctic question; the plan carries into the neighboring-country research of social studies grade 4 unit 2 (ss4-canada-mexico-research), whose project sits in weeks 5 to 8, kept to land, climate and animals; no question about a people, a culture or a border (K to 5 neutral rule). Stand-alone: "How do Arctic animals get through the winter?" with the Arctic overview, the three printed kinds and an answering passage for each entry (Curio Class writes all). The judge step brings back grade 3's maker and purpose; the source line brings back the grade 3 source list. Stop rule on any search (close, tell, no blame); printed kinds or a teacher-checked page only (APPROACH Sensitive ground items 2 and 3). Self-check: each student rates their use of the skill card's steps, names one step done well and one thing to do differently next time. Working notes in the research notebook. Whose voices: the sources record their makers (C12).

goal: End-of-unit assessment, written sitting (about 25 minutes for 30): from a new broad topic and a short overview, a narrowed part, two or three questions with a guess and a plan whose sources fit them; then a search plan for one question carried out across two of three new printed kinds, one located result from each recorded, and what each kind was good for
note: New topic (an invented one on how deserts stay cool at night), not seen in the unit. Rubric (teacher-judged): the part is narrower than the topic, the questions fit it, the plan's sources fit its questions, and the plan names what I still do not know, and each step fills one of those (I.B.2 and I.A.1); the search plan uses two kinds, each try shows what it found and what that kind was good for (IV.B.1). Taken without the card. Response time: day 6.

goal: Respond: regrouped reteach by the rubric step missed (the narrowed part, questions that fit, a plan that fits, or a search try that records what it found), ending with one fresh try
note: Groups from the class record sheet (APPROACH unit field 7); the reteach uses day 1's or day 2's show-me case. No readiness check before unit 2: every row it assumes was used in library grade 3 and is retrieved on its days 8 to 10.

goal: Show-me: the hook and the compelling question, then the teacher reads a beaver passage with the research question beside it, notes only the facts that answer it in own words, marks an opinion as opinion, crosses out "interesting but not an answer" facts, sorts the notes into boxes the teacher names and explains, and says what the notes show
note: Skill card "question beside me, answer only, my words, my boxes; first-hand or about it, why made; my words, a few in marks, say where", held by the teacher. Hook: a photo of a beaver dam with a pond behind it. Candidate kept: the details that answer, and one line "what my notes show" as a conclusion from them, modeled here (about 2 minutes). The model may start from a grade 3 key-word box as the "before" picture, inside the show-me, not as a task. ELA grade 4 unit 1 (e4-evidence-inference, weeks 1 to 8) came before; today still names "the detail that answers" itself. Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): cross out the facts that do not answer on a short new paragraph.

goal: Show-me: a primary and a secondary source on the same beaver pond (a wildlife worker's field log and a book passage), what each can tell that the other cannot, four invented pages sorted by purpose (inform, persuade, sell, entertain) with the ad found, and one statement on an invented page checked against a second source and marked supported, contradicted or not settled
note: Opens with the five-minute retrieval task: label two sources primary or secondary and name each maker (g3-source-kinds-and-makers, library grade 3), before the comparison that builds on it. Begun here, owned in grade 5 (g5-first-lateral-check, g5-choose-sources). Social studies grade 4 unit 4 (ss4-primary-source, weeks 12 to 16) and ELA grade 4 unit 4 (e4-firsthand-secondhand, weeks 24 to 32) come at the end of this unit or later: today teaches the primary and secondary comparison itself on beaver cases and borrows none of social studies' voyages and conquest content (K to 5 neutral rule). The ad page sells an invented product with no brand. Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): say what one new primary source can tell that a book cannot.

goal: Show-me with practice: honest use modeled (an idea put in own words, a few exact words in quotation marks with the source, saying where it came from, and why a maker cares), then pairs sort four case cards into honest and not yet honest and fix the second kind
note: Opens with the five-minute retrieval task: a source list line for one cover, title, author, year and kind (g3-source-list, library grade 3), before honest use and the source list. Sensitivity: honest use without shaming (APPROACH Sensitive ground item 4); the case cards are invented students, never a classmate, and a student whose notes copy a sentence is helped privately. ELA grade 4 unit 2 (e4-research, weeks 8 to 16) runs the same weeks; this day teaches honest use and the source list itself. Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): fix one not-yet-honest case and say why.

goal: Practice: pairs with the card take answer-only notes from a new passage into boxes they name, sort four new invented pages by purpose and mark the ad, and fix two more not-yet-honest cases, with feedback after each round; the exit ticket checks one statement on an invented page against a second source
note: Opens with the five-minute retrieval task: two key-word notes from a short paragraph (g3-notes-in-boxes, library grade 3), before the own-box notes round. Every move was shown on days 7 to 9. Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): mark one statement on a new invented page supported, contradicted or not settled by a second supplied source (the continuum's grade 4 media accuracy cell, from the band file on disk, read by the frame and checked by the expert 2026-11-26; its store entry waits on later.csv L149).

goal: Inquiry: for the host question, answer-only notes from a primary and a secondary source into the student's own labeled boxes, one line on where the two sources differ, one line on what the notes show, a source list, a pair share of the answer, then the self-check
note: Card withdrawn today. Minutes: notes about 13, the two lines about 4, source list about 3, share about 3, self-check about 4. Stand-alone: "What do beavers do to a stream when they build a dam?" with the beaver set (a wildlife worker's field log, a photo with caption, two book passages; Curio Class writes all). Host: ELA grade 4 unit 2's animal defenses research (e4-research, weeks 8 to 16) is the in-step host; where both run, one set of notes may serve both. Science grade 4 unit 2's energy resources question (s4-energy-resources) ended in week 10 and may be reused as a finished question, kept to how a resource is made and used, not to policy. Candidates kept: one "where the sources differ" line (a fact, a count or a date, about 2 minutes) and the "what my notes show" line (about 2 minutes). The search plan comes back as one try for the second source. Self-check: each student rates their use of the skill card's steps, names one step done well and one thing to do differently next time. Whose voices: the sources record their makers (C12).

goal: End-of-unit assessment, written sitting (about 27 minutes for 30): a new passage and question, notes that keep only the answers in own words sorted into the student's own labeled boxes with the plan said; one line on what a new primary and a new secondary source can each tell, three invented pages sorted by purpose with the ad marked and one statement checked against a second source; two not-yet-honest cases fixed with a reason
note: New case (an invented passage on how otters keep warm). Parts: notes rubric, about 12 minutes (I.B.1 keeps the answers, IV.B.4 own boxes with the plan said); items, about 7 minutes (IV.A.3 what each kind can tell, IV.B.3 purpose, the ad and the accuracy check, the second source given as two printed sentences beside the statement so the 7 minutes hold); honest-use rubric, about 8 minutes (VI.A.2). Taken without the card. Response time: day 13.

goal: Respond: regrouped reteach by the step missed (answer-only notes, own boxes, kind and purpose, or an honest-use fix), ending with one fresh try
note: Groups from the class record sheet. The class count of students meeting each rubric step is written on the mid-year check's sheet (day 14).

goal: Mid-year course-level check, written sitting (about 25 minutes for 30), drawing its items from unit 1: a narrowed part of a new broad topic, two questions with a guess and a plan whose sources fit them, and a search plan across two new printed kinds saying what each was good for
note: Week 14. New case (an invented topic on how penguins raise chicks; new printed kinds). Rubric as day 5's, with the line "the plan names what I still do not know, and each step fills one of those" (I.B.2). Unit 2, which ended the week before, is not re-tested: its end-of-unit result is carried unscored as a class count of the students who met each rubric step, written on this sheet. The unit 1 sitting was week 5, so no task form repeats within two weeks.

goal: Respond: small-group reteach of the missed step from the mid-year sheet, ending with one fresh try
note: Week 15. Groups by the step missed on day 14; a group whose class count on unit 2 shows a missed step works that step instead. No readiness check before unit 3: g3-research-team was used in library grade 3 and is retrieved on day 17.

goal: Show-me: the hook and the compelling question, a question no book can answer yet, then the teacher plans two new ways to find out with a sample group (a class survey on which of three read-aloud books to hear again, and a week-long observation of the schoolyard after rain), writing the steps, what to collect and how to tally it
note: Skill card "no source? plan a new way, steps, collect, tally; open question, listen, record", held by the teacher. Hook: three read-aloud covers and "Which one do we want again? No book can tell us." Sensitivity: survey rules (APPROACH Sensitive ground item 8): a neutral class question checked by the teacher; no question about family, home, beliefs, identity, health, money, food or meals; no names on a survey. The tally uses grade 3 math (scaled graphs), the year before. Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): say whether a new question needs a source, a survey or an observation, and why.

goal: Show-me with practice: open and closed questions, asking a classmate or a school adult how they see a topic, listening without arguing, restating the answer and recording it; then pairs rewrite four closed questions as open ones and write the steps of a plan for one new case
note: Opens with the five-minute retrieval task: name what each of three sample team members added (g3-research-team, library grade 3). Candidate kept: restating another's idea accurately before adding one's own, modeled here and a "what they said" line on the interview record (about 2 minutes). Interview rules: any school adult, inside school, on a neutral topic the teacher approved; answers recorded by role, never by full name. Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): rewrite one closed question as open.

goal: Inquiry: groups run the class survey or start the observation (a set spot or a window, with the teacher), each member doing a named step; pairs ask a classmate or a school adult their three open questions, listen and record
note: The observation runs for a week between sessions: the classroom teacher runs the daily two-minute look and a student records it on the observation sheet, which goes home on the paper path. Host, in step: the changing land unit of science grade 4 unit 4 (weeks 15 to 19), for example how rain moves soil in the schoolyard; stand-alone: "Which read-aloud book does our class most want to hear again?" At home (one student and the teaching adult): the printed sequence of invented schoolyard pictures after rain (which places stay wet longest), what to record, a tally, and three open questions to the adult, with the same rubric steps. The plan's steps bring back unit 1's plan (one line: do the steps fit the question?). If no rain falls or the ground is frozen, the observation group records what the week offers at three set spots (where frost, puddles or snow last longest), or works from the printed schoolyard picture sequence in class; the steps and the tally are the same. Working notes in the research notebook.

goal: Inquiry with share: groups tally the survey or the week's observation into one class result, say what the plan found and why it answers the question, pairs report one interview answer accurately, then the self-check
note: Candidate kept: working with a group to make a shared result, as one class tally chart each group adds to (about 3 minutes). A tally and a bar graph use grade 3 math only. Self-check: each student rates their use of the skill card's steps, names one step done well and one thing to do differently next time. Whose voices: the unit records who answered, by role, never by name (C12). Leans on the continuum's 3 to 5 band file, on disk, read by the frame and checked by the expert 2026-11-26 (its store entry waits on later.csv L149).

goal: End-of-unit assessment (about 28 minutes for 30): a written part, all at once, explaining the group's plan and why it answers the question, saying for a new neutral question no source holds which kind of plan to use and its first step, and writing three open questions for a new neutral topic; then observed exchanges, about 70 seconds a pair for 15 pairs while the others finish writing: each student asks one open question, restates the partner's answer and asks one follow-up
note: Written part about 10 minutes (the new-question line about 2), observed part about 18. The teacher records the three exchange results separately (open question, accurate restatement, follow-up); the written record supports the observation. V.C.2 is the plan explained and a plan chosen for a new question; II.D.2 the open questions and the exchange (an observed performance); II.A.1 the restatement. Topics teacher-approved and neutral. Taken without the card. Response time: day 21.

goal: Respond: regrouped reteach by the step missed (a plan that answers, open questions, or restating and following up), ending with one fresh try
note: Groups from the class record sheet. No readiness check before unit 4: g3-make-product and g3-gallery-feedback were used in library grade 3 and are retrieved on days 23 and 25.

goal: Show-me: the hook and the compelling question, then the teacher thinks aloud choosing a question of their own from a wonder or the neutral list just to learn, names who the "I found out" sheet is for before choosing its form, and each student chooses a question and writes the audience line
note: Skill card "my question, my plan, my sheet; advice, choose, change, log", held by the teacher. Hook: a jar of honey and "How did bees make this?" Candidate kept: choosing a form for an audience and a purpose, as the audience line (about 2 minutes). Sensitivity: questions stay on neutral ground; the teacher steers a sensitive choice privately to a nearby neutral one, never in front of the class. Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): say who the sheet is for and which form suits them.

goal: Inquiry: each student writes a plan for their own question and searches across two kinds in the general source set, recording what each kind gave
note: Opens with the five-minute retrieval task: find the sentence in a sample product not backed by its notes (g3-make-product, library grade 3). Unit 1's plan and search come back as review. The general source set of short passages on the list's topics (Curio Class writes all). A student whose question no source answers may plan a survey or ask a school adult, as in unit 3. Stop rule on any search (close, tell, no blame); printed kinds or a teacher-checked page only (APPROACH Sensitive ground items 2 and 3).

goal: Inquiry: answer-only notes and the draft "I found out" sheet with its source list; the class reads the rubric beside a sample sheet before drafting, and each student checks the draft against it and marks one change it needs
note: Candidate kept: what makes a good product, as the rubric read beside a sample before drafting (about 4 minutes); the rubric self-check is the continuum's grade 4 self-assessment cell (from the band file on disk, read by the frame and checked by the expert 2026-11-26; its store entry waits on later.csv L149). Unit 2's notes and honest use come back as review; a copied sentence is fixed privately. ELA grade 4 unit 1 (e4-writing-process, weeks 1 to 8) came before.

goal: Feedback round: pairs read each other's draft sheet and leave two notes on the skill card's slip, one thing it taught them and one specific, kind piece of advice about the work
note: Opens with the five-minute retrieval task: one specific, kind suggestion on a sample sheet (g3-gallery-feedback, library grade 3). Partners assigned by the teacher so every sheet gets notes. The teacher reads the slips before they reach their owner; advice stays kind and about the work.

goal: Show-me with revision: the teacher thinks aloud choosing which advice to use on a sample sheet and fills the change log (advice, what I changed, or why I kept it); then each student chooses, revises their sheet and keeps their own log
note: The change log is new today. Card withdrawn at the end of the session. Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): one log line for one piece of advice on a sample sheet.

goal: End-of-unit assessment: the revised "I found out" sheet and its change log handed in and scored on their rubric, then a written sitting (about 15 minutes for 30) on a new sample sheet with three pieces of advice: choose which to use, write the log lines and make one change
note: First about 12 minutes: students finish and hand in the revised sheet and log. Sheet rubric: the question is the student's own and the sheet answers it (V.A.3), the log matches the changes (I.C.3); the sitting rubric covers I.C.3 on a new case. Taken without the card. Response time: day 28.

goal: Share, reteach and self-check: the revised sheets in a class gallery (about 15 minutes), the regrouped reteach from the sheet and sitting rubrics (about 10 minutes), then the self-check (about 4 minutes)
note: The unit's respond step (frame). Candidate kept: presenting with care for content and delivery, as one gallery line "is my answer easy to find?" (about 1 minute). Self-check: each student rates their use of the skill card's steps, names one step done well and one thing to do differently next time. Whose voices: the sheets' source lists record their makers (C12).

goal: Year-end course-level check, written sitting (about 27 minutes for 30), drawing its items from units 1 to 3: a plan for a new topic; answer-only notes from a short passage into the student's own boxes, three invented pages sorted by purpose and one not-yet-honest case fixed with a reason; three open questions for a new topic and one line on why a survey or an observation answers a question no source holds
